# US-05.3 — Reject unsafe uploads before spending cloud budget

|                  |                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-05 FastAPI Core Service & Agentic Controller](../epics/EPIC-05-api-service.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                                   |
| **Estimate**     | 2                                                                                    |
| **Status**       | Blocked                                                                              |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                      |
| **Files**        | [backend/main.py](../../../backend/main.py)                                          |
| **Backlog ID**   | STORY-011 (EPIC-005)                                                                 |
| **Requirements** | [FR-16](../../../agile/requirements.md); FR-15 temperature handling; NFR-7           |

## User story

**As an** operator,
**I want** unsupported and oversized uploads rejected at the API boundary,
**so that** invalid requests cannot consume cloud budget or overwhelm analysis with unbounded input.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Unsupported media rejected**
Given an upload whose content type is not `image/png`, `image/jpeg` or `image/webp`,
when I submit it to analysis,
then HTTP 415 is returned before any telemetry, Gemini, Firestore, Pub/Sub or GCS call.

**AC2 — Actual bytes determine size rejection**
Given the actual uploaded image exceeds the agreed 10 MB limit, whose exact byte value is `TBD (OQ-2)`, regardless of absent or misleading size headers,
when I submit it,
then HTTP 413 is returned before any cloud call.

**AC3 — Exact boundary is accepted**
Given a supported upload containing exactly the agreed maximum number of bytes, `TBD (OQ-2)`,
when I submit it with otherwise valid inputs,
then size validation accepts it, while maximum-plus-one byte is rejected with HTTP 413.

**AC4 — Temperature fallback is deliberate**
Given an absent temperature or one outside the plausible Celsius range, `TBD (OQ-2)`,
when I submit an otherwise accepted upload,
then telemetry supplies the report temperature instead of forwarding implausible input to Gemini; malformed non-numeric form input returns HTTP 422 before cloud work.

## Tasks

- [x] Read uploaded bytes in the async route
- [ ] Restrict accepted content types to PNG, JPEG and WebP
- [ ] Enforce the agreed byte ceiling against actual bytes read, not only request headers
- [ ] Reject unsafe uploads before invoking every cloud dependency
- [ ] Apply the agreed temperature plausibility policy and preserve telemetry fallback semantics
- [ ] Add negative media, byte-boundary, forged-header and no-cloud-call assertions

## Current state

No MIME or size validation exists. The current unbounded `await file.read()` is not enforcement of a byte ceiling. No ambient temperature field is accepted. STORY-011 is blocked on foundation prerequisites and unresolved OQ-2.

| Gap                                                  | Impact                                                                                                 |
| ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Every content type is accepted and size is unchecked | Unsupported and oversized requests reach cloud orchestration                                           |
| No actual-byte ceiling                               | Client headers cannot prove a request is within budget                                                 |
| OQ-2 has no human answer                             | Tests cannot choose between 10,000,000 and 10,485,760 bytes or define plausible temperature boundaries |

The backlog priority is P1; the older epic's P0 label is not copied or changed here. The [FastAPI instructions](../../instructions/fastapi-backend.instructions.md) require 415/413 before cloud calls and fallback for missing or implausible temperature, not a newly invented numeric range or an automatic 422 for every implausible numeric value. Scan history limits are owned by STORY-013 and STORY-006, not this upload slice.

## Test cases

| Test                                                              | Asserts                                                                        |
| ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `test_unsupported_upload_returns_415_without_cloud_calls`         | All unsupported media fail before every mocked dependency                      |
| `test_oversized_upload_returns_413_using_actual_bytes`            | Misleading or missing size headers cannot bypass the agreed limit              |
| `test_upload_size_boundary_accepts_maximum_rejects_one_more`      | Exact byte-boundary semantics; blocked until OQ-2 is answered                  |
| `test_temperature_validation_uses_agreed_range_and_safe_fallback` | Missing/implausible numeric input selects telemetry and malformed input is 422 |

## Definition of done

OQ-2 defines both the exact byte ceiling and plausible Celsius range, all four cases pass with cloud-call spies, supported media within the limit reach normal orchestration, and coverage meets the 70% floor. No undocumented limit is chosen to make tests pass.
